title: stage-back runs an item's checks before the staged file is committed, so a check that measures a clone of HEAD sees the old file
goal: stage-back commits the copies, then runs the item's own checks over that commit, so a check that clones the worktree's HEAD reads the staged file; a failing check makes stage-back exit 1 and undo the commit, so work/ID, the worktree and its file are as they were before the run; `stage-back ID --check` still commits nothing and leaves the worktree as it was

run:
import hashlib, json, os, pathlib, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

TOOL = str(pathlib.Path("_tools/backlog.py").resolve())
ID, REL = "TK-stagebck", ".claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md"
GIT = ["git", "-c", "user.name=fixture", "-c", "user.email=fixture"]


def git(cwd, *args):
    return subprocess.run(GIT + list(args), cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


def build(base, want):
    """A throwaway repo with the item TK-stagebck on work/TK-stagebck in its worktree, a staging copy of REL
    ("staged") under its scratch directory, and the item's check: clone HEAD of the worktree, read REL there, write
    what it read to a sentinel file and exit 0 only when that equals WANT."""
    fix, sentinel = pathlib.Path(base, "clone"), pathlib.Path(base, "seen.txt")
    check = ("import pathlib, subprocess, sys, tempfile\n"
             "with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:\n"
             "    subprocess.run(['git', 'clone', '-q', '.', d + '/c'], check=True)\n"
             f"    seen = pathlib.Path(d, 'c', {REL!r}).read_text()\n"
             f"pathlib.Path({str(sentinel)!r}).write_text(seen)\n"
             f"sys.exit(0 if seen == {want!r} else 1)\n")
    item = {"id": ID, "kind": "task", "title": "fixture item", "status": "doing", "touches": [REL],
            "checks": [{"run": ["python3", "-c", check]}]}
    (fix / "_backlog").mkdir(parents=True)
    (fix / "backlog.json").write_text(json.dumps({"item_dir": "_backlog"}), encoding="utf-8")
    (fix / "_backlog" / f"{ID}.json").write_text(json.dumps(item, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (fix / REL).parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    (fix / REL).write_text("old", encoding="utf-8")
    git(fix, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    git(fix, "config", "user.name", "fixture")  # stage-back's own commit reads the repository's identity
    git(fix, "config", "user.email", "fixture")
    git(fix, "add", "-A")
    git(fix, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
    wt = fix / ".claude" / "worktrees" / f"agent-{ID}"
    git(fix, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", f"work/{ID}", str(wt))
    scratch = fix / "_cache" / "scratch" / ID
    (scratch / "staging" / REL).parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    (scratch / "staging" / REL).write_text("staged", encoding="utf-8")
    (scratch / "staging-bases.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({REL: hashlib.sha256(b"old").hexdigest()}, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return fix, wt, sentinel


def stage_back(base, fix, *flags):
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "KB_BACKLOG_CONFIG"}
    env.update(CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=str(pathlib.Path(base, "data")), CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=str(pathlib.Path.cwd()),
               KB_COORD_STORE=str(pathlib.Path(base, "coord.sqlite")))
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, TOOL, "--root", str(fix), "stage-back", ID, *flags], capture_output=True,
                       text=True, env=env)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout + p.stderr


def head(wt):
    return git(wt, "rev-parse", "HEAD")


def driven():
    """The staged copy is checked by a check that reads a clone of HEAD: it must see the staged file."""
    base = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stage-back-fixture-")
    try:
        fix, wt, sentinel = build(base, "staged")
        before = head(wt)
        code, out = stage_back(base, fix)
        seen = sentinel.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if sentinel.exists() else None
        assert seen == "staged", f"the check saw {seen!r}, not the staged file (stage-back exit {code}):\n{out[-600:]}"
        assert code == 0, f"stage-back exit {code}:\n{out[-600:]}"
        assert git(wt, "rev-list", "--count", f"{before}..HEAD") == "1", "stage-back did not leave one commit"
        assert git(wt, "show", f"HEAD:{REL}") == "staged", "the commit does not hold the staged file"
        assert git(wt, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no") == "", "the worktree is dirty after the commit"
        print("driven case: the check read the staged file in a clone of HEAD, one commit holds it")
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)


def planted():
    """A failing check: stage-back exits 1 and leaves the branch, the worktree and its file as they were. --check
    commits nothing either."""
    base = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stage-back-fixture-")
    try:
        fix, wt, sentinel = build(base, "never")
        before = head(wt)
        code, out = stage_back(base, fix, "--check")
        assert code == 0 and head(wt) == before and (wt / REL).read_text() == "old", f"--check changed the worktree:\n{out[-600:]}"
        code, out = stage_back(base, fix)
        assert code == 1, f"a failing check gave exit {code}, not 1:\n{out[-600:]}"
        assert head(wt) == before, "a failing check left a commit on the branch"
        assert git(fix, "rev-parse", f"work/{ID}") == before, "the branch moved"
        assert (wt / REL).read_text() == "old", "the worktree file is not the one it was"
        assert git(wt, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no") == "", "the worktree is dirty"
        assert (fix / "_cache" / "scratch" / ID / "staging" / REL).read_text() == "staged", "the staging copy changed"
        print("planted case: a failing check left the branch, the worktree and its file as they were")
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)


driven()
if "all" in sys.argv[1:]:
    planted()

gates.question: How does stage-back let an item's own checks read the staged file in a clone of the worktree's HEAD?
options: commit the copies first, run the checks over that commit and undo it when one fails
run the checks that read a clone of HEAD only at done and name them in stage-back's output
gates.recommendation: commit the copies first, run the checks over that commit and undo it when one fails
gates.reason: stage-back cannot tell which checks read a clone of HEAD, so a deferral has no mechanical test, and a failing check still leaves the branch and the worktree as they were
gates.answer: commit the copies first, run the checks over that commit and undo it when one fails

gates.question: How does stage-back take its commit off when an item check fails after it?
options: reset the branch to its pre-commit HEAD with git reset --mixed, then put each original file back
git reset --hard to the pre-commit HEAD
gates.recommendation: reset the branch to its pre-commit HEAD with git reset --mixed, then put each original file back
gates.answer: reset the branch to its pre-commit HEAD with git reset --mixed, then put each original file back

notes: Premise: cmd_stage_back copies the staging copies into the worktree, runs stage_back_checks over the uncommitted files and commits after, so an item check that clones the worktree's HEAD reads the last commit's file. Repro on the base: exit 1, AssertionError: the check saw 'old', not the staged file (stage-back exit 1); stage-back printed: refused: 1 copy(ies), worktree as it was, nothing committed. Design (goal follows the recommended option of gate g1): copy-in, selfdoc.py check and selfdoc.py stale --since HEAD stay before the commit (the stale list and the Self-Reviewed trailer need the copies uncommitted); then the commit; then the item's checks and repro over it, in the loop stage_back_checks has now; a failing check undoes the commit (restore_originals) and exits 1; an error after the commit must not leave it either; --check stops after the selfdoc part. With the other option the goal, repro and check are reshaped first: the repro asserts a check ran over the staged file, which that option never does. The check runs the repro's driven case and a planted case: a failing item check (clones HEAD, exits 1) leaves work/ID, the worktree file and the staging copy as they were; stage-back --check commits nothing. About 2 s. On a patched copy of bl_dispatch.py that commits first and resets one commit on a failure both cases pass; on the base the driven case fails and the planted case alone passes. referrers: bl_dispatch.py is the one kind=ref file; backlog.py, bl_land.py, bl_runs.py, kb_mcp.py only name the command. Docs: tools.md (stage-back, dispatch, bl_dispatch.py rows), backlog.md (stage-back paragraph), skills/sprint/SKILL.md (kb-sprint links to it). Overlap: those three docs are in other sessions' plans; s-1d406b asked (Ae3cf1657eb) about the sprint skill's stage-back sentence; edit only the stage-back lines.
